learningObjective: Distinguish constant folding from constant propagation and identify when folding is legal.

canonicalClaims.claim: Constant folding evaluates operations whose operands are compile-time constants at compile time, producing a new constant, while preserving source semantics for overflow, rounding, and floating-point edge cases (NaN, ±Inf).
conditions: All operands are known at compile time.
The operation's semantics permit compile-time evaluation without changing observable behavior.
nonImplications: Does not imply folding is unconditional; special values (NaN, Inf, div-by-zero) may block folding.
Does not imply folding requires SSA; it works in non-SSA IRs too.

misconceptions.claim: Constant folding and constant propagation are synonyms.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Folding evaluates a constant expression; propagation substitutes a known constant value for a use site. They can be applied together.

misconceptions.claim: IEEE-754 arithmetic is associative, so constant folding may freely reassociate expressions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: IEEE-754 addition and multiplication are NOT associative; naive reassociation changes rounding behavior. -ffast-math opts into unsafe reassociation.
Folding evaluates local constant expressions; SSA is not required, though it makes downstream propagation easier.

implementationFacts: LLVM ConstantFolding pass folds arithmetic, bitwise, and known-safe FP operations.
Sparse Conditional Constant Propagation (SCCP) combines propagation with reachability analysis for improved precision.
performanceScenarios: Front-end constant folding removes template/inline overhead in C++; downstream ML compilers rely on it to simplify shape computations.
